+//! The cached threading-cycle record (issue #34, `crate::cl::ThreadCycle`)
+//! in the project file. Our own format; the additive law of the comps
+//! and notes keys: absent is none - every non-threading path, and every
+//! cache before the record existed.
+
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+use crate::cl::{lattice, Move, ThreadCycle};
+use crate::geometry::Point3;
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct ThreadCycleDto {
+    pub start: [f64; 3],
+    pub end: [f64; 3],
+    pub major_diameter: f64,
+    pub minor_diameter: f64,
+    pub lead: f64,
+    pub height: f64,
+    pub first_depth: f64,
+    pub min_depth: f64,
+    pub finish_allowance: f64,
+    pub infeed_angle: f64,
+    pub spring_passes: u32,
+    pub pull_out: f64,
+    pub first: u64,
+    pub last: u64,
+}
+
+impl ThreadCycleDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_cycle(t: &ThreadCycle) -> Self {
+        // The points take the lattice snap `MoveDto` gives the moves
+        // they sit on, so the record still opens on its move on load.
+        let lat = |p: Point3| [lattice(p.x), lattice(p.y), lattice(p.z)];
+        ThreadCycleDto {
+            start: lat(t.start),
+            end: lat(t.end),
+            major_diameter: t.major_diameter,
+            minor_diameter: t.minor_diameter,
+            lead: t.lead,
+            height: t.height,
+            first_depth: t.first_depth,
+            min_depth: t.min_depth,
+            finish_allowance: t.finish_allowance,
+            infeed_angle: t.infeed_angle,
+            spring_passes: t.spring_passes,
+            pull_out: t.pull_out,
+            first: t.first as u64,
+            last: t.last as u64,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The record over the loaded moves - `None` when it does not sit
+    /// on them (the file's bytes are the law, the sanity door is the
+    /// reader's: the passes then post as themselves).
+    pub(super) fn to_cycle(&self, moves: &[Move]) -> Option<ThreadCycle> {
+        let t = ThreadCycle {
+            start: Point3::new(self.start[0], self.start[1], self.start[2]),
+            end: Point3::new(self.end[0], self.end[1], self.end[2]),
+            major_diameter: self.major_diameter,
+            minor_diameter: self.minor_diameter,
+            lead: self.lead,
+            height: self.height,
+            first_depth: self.first_depth,
+            min_depth: self.min_depth,
+            finish_allowance: self.finish_allowance,
+            infeed_angle: self.infeed_angle,
+            spring_passes: self.spring_passes,
+            pull_out: self.pull_out,
+            first: usize::try_from(self.first).unwrap_or(usize::MAX),
+            last: usize::try_from(self.last).unwrap_or(usize::MAX),
+        };
+        t.is_sane(moves).then_some(t)
+    }
+}

+//! The threading intent record (issue #34): what a thread's cycle is,
+//! standing beside the explicit helical passes that cut it.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the quantities a lathe control's multi-pass threading
+//! cycle asks for - start and end of the thread, major / minor
+//! diameter, lead, thread height, first-pass and minimum depth, finish
+//! allowance, infeed angle, spring passes, pull-out - as public lathe
+//! programming references and machine-tool handbooks list them
+//! (behaviour only). Our own model; no vendor material consulted. The
+//! explicit passes remain the truth for verification, display and
+//! simulation (the drilling `Cycle` law); the record is what a post
+//! with a threading cycle writes in their place.
+
+use crate::geometry::Point3;
+
+use super::moves::Move;
+
+/// One thread's machining intent: the passes `moves[first..=last]`
+/// are what the machine does in G32 form; a cycle-capable post writes
+/// one threading cycle from these numbers instead. Points are world
+/// coordinates on the stream's lattice; lengths are mm, radial
+/// quantities are RADIUS values.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct ThreadCycle {
+    /// The cycle's start point: clearance radius, thread start station
+    /// (the tool returns here after every pass).
+    pub start: Point3,
+    /// The thread's end at the root: minor radius, last station.
+    pub end: Point3,
+    /// Crest diameter (2 x the blank's crest radius in the window).
+    pub major_diameter: f64,
+    /// Root diameter (2 x the deepest pass's tip radius).
+    pub minor_diameter: f64,
+    /// Axial travel per spindle revolution (single start: the pitch).
+    pub lead: f64,
+    /// Thread height, radial (crest to root).
+    pub height: f64,
+    /// Depth of the first pass, radial.
+    pub first_depth: f64,
+    /// The smallest depth increment a pass may take, radial.
+    pub min_depth: f64,
+    /// Radial stock the finishing pass removes (0: the last roughing
+    /// rung is the root).
+    pub finish_allowance: f64,
+    /// Included angle of the compound infeed, degrees; 0 is straight
+    /// radial infeed (every pass plunges square to the axis).
+    pub infeed_angle: f64,
+    /// Extra passes at full depth after the finishing pass.
+    pub spring_passes: u32,
+    /// Axial length of the angled pull-out at the thread's end (0: a
+    /// square, radial retract).
+    pub pull_out: f64,
+    /// The passes' first move (the rapid onto the start point).
+    pub first: usize,
+    /// The passes' last move (the retract after the deepest pass),
+    /// inclusive.
+    pub last: usize,
+}
+
+impl ThreadCycle {
+    /// Does the record sit on a path of these moves: an in-range span
+    /// opening on its start point and finite numbers that state a
+    /// thread? The door the dump and the loader check before trusting
+    /// a record; out-of-range CYCLE words are the post's to refuse.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn is_sane(&self, moves: &[Move]) -> bool {
+        let (Some(m0), Some(_)) = (moves.get(self.first), moves.get(self.last)) else {
+            return false;
+        };
+        let nums = [
+            self.major_diameter,
+            self.minor_diameter,
+            self.lead,
+            self.height,
+            self.first_depth,
+            self.min_depth,
+            self.finish_allowance,
+            self.infeed_angle,
+            self.pull_out,
+        ];
+        self.first <= self.last
+            && m0.to == self.start
+            && self.start.is_finite()
+            && self.end.is_finite()
+            && nums.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite())
+            && self.lead > 0.0
+            && self.height > 0.0
+    }
+}

+<!-- moved from RECOMMENDED.md by PR #211 (docs/decisions rule, PR #250) -->
+
+## #34 - G76 threading on the Fanuc Lathe post, from a thread-cycle record in the stream (2026-11-08)
+
+Lifts the M13.5 "G32, not G76" limit ("the first lathe post" entry).
+
+**The record rides beside the passes, not instead of them.** The thread
+kernel keeps its explicit helical passes (the sim, verify and every G32
+program read them, unchanged) and adds one `cl::ThreadCycle` per thread
+(`Toolpath.threads`): start point (clearance radius, first centre), end
+at the root on the last centre, major / minor diameter, lead, thread
+height, first-pass and minimum depth, finish allowance, infeed angle,
+spring passes, pull-out, and the move span `first..=last` it stands
+for - the drilling `Cycle` law (intent beside the expanded chain), with
+a sanity door (`is_sane`: in range, opens on its own move) read by the
+dump and the project loader. The stream carries it as `THREAD ...` /
+`THREAD END` around the passes; the cache as an additive `threads` key.
+Dropped: a CL-only cycle with no passes (the sim and verify would need a
+second reading of the same thread), and re-deriving the cycle from the
+G32 arcs in the script (the "re-deriving is what the record replaces"
+law).
+
+**The kernel's honest numbers.** The ladder plunges RADIALLY in equal
+rungs of `infeed` to the root, so the record says infeed angle 0, first
+depth = minimum depth = the rung, no finish allowance, no spring pass,
+square pull-out. Under Fanuc's G76 depth law (n-th cut at d*sqrt(n),
+increments clamped to dmin) dmin = d makes every increment the rung - the
+control cuts the kernel's own ladder. `m` = 1 + spring passes (the
+finishing repetition count is at least one), so G76 runs one finishing
+pass at full depth the explicit passes do not show - a spring pass, no
+deeper than the root the verdict judged. Flank or modified-flank infeed,
+finish allowance and pull-out are record fields the kernel does not set
+yet; the post already writes and range-checks them.
+
+**The choice is a document post option, default G32.** A new singleton
+`PostOptions { threading: G32Passes | G76Cycle }`, moved only by the
+undoable `SetPostOptions` (UI: a "Threading" combo under the post picker
+while Fanuc Lathe is the post), persisted as an additive `post_options`
+key (absent = default, no version bump - the comps law), handed to the
+script as the global `postOptions` by `engine::run_with` (`run` and the
+CLI pass none = every default). Default G32 keeps every existing golden
+byte-identical, and a script without `onThreadCycle` (every mill post)
+ignores the record. Dropped: a per-op threading parameter (the cycle is
+a dialect choice of the post, not of the cut), and a stream PARAM (it
+would change every stream golden).
+
+**G76 words** (public Fanuc 0i-T style lathe documentation, behaviour
+only): `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X(root dia) Z(end) P(k)
+Q(first depth) F(lead)` after one positioning rapid to the start point;
+Q/P in whole microns (radius values), R in mm, X diameter, F mm/rev; R(i)
+taper omitted (the kernel threads plumb only). Refused by name, never
+posted as G32 under a G76 choice: passes with no record ("regenerate the
+thread, or choose G32 passes"), an infeed angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80,
+spring passes over 98, a pull-out that is not 0..9.9 leads in tenths,
+first/minimum depth outside the height, a finish allowance at or over it,
+an internal thread (minor >= major), an end off the minor diameter, a
+start inside the crest, no lead, no length. Golden:
+`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`.
